kill_argument: Nothing in this paper is new evidence about the return to schooling, and the one test that bears on Card's basic specification came out as the design predicted from published numbers before any run: the reduced-form t of about 2.5 is below the chi-square(3) projection value, so the robust set [-0.0068, 0.4983] was bound to contain zero. The exact replication was already published by Kling (2001); the Panel A results are restatements of a reduced-form t on a coefficient the paper itself says cannot be the return; the H3(b) comparison added at this stage shows only that the conservative projection, not the data, separates the robust and homoskedastic answers, and the size-correct robust subvector test that would settle it was not run. A referee could fairly call this a careful audit with no answer. What I attacked that held: every paper-r1 fix in the files; claims.jsonl values, supports and macros unchanged since 569bc72; the D8 diff is two label strings and fig-chr metrics equal the superseded run's; units, counts, balance N and title; validate --strict clean; PDF newer than its sources. Still required for submission: the clean rerun, then regenerate process.tex and the PDF.

findings.text: Unit error in the abstract and elsewhere: 0.0114 is in units of log wage, i.e. about 1.1 log points, but the abstract, the introduction and Section 4.4 say proximity may raise log wages 'by 0.0114 log points', and Table 4 labels the breakdown '(log points)'. The paper contradicts itself two paragraphs later ('a direct effect of about one log point', also in the conclusion). Same error in Section 4.1: '0.1324 log points correspond to a 14.2% higher hourly wage' (0.1324 is 13.2 log points), introduced as 'In real units', which suggests inflation adjustment; it is a percent conversion of a point estimate whose robust set contains zero. Remedy: 'by 0.0114 (about 1.1 log points)' or 'by 0.0114 in log wage'; 'a coefficient of 0.1324 corresponds to a 14.2% wage difference'; fix the table label. The claim texts of a6-/a5-pacoef-chr-breakdown and plan.json H4 carry the same '(log points)' wording.

findings.text: The H3(b) reading understates evidence already in the ledger. The paper says the robust set contains zero 'possibly because the projection is conservative'. h3b-subvector also wrote b6_kappap_at_zero = 6.836, the homoskedastic subvector AR statistic at b0 = 0 on the chi-square scale (it equals 3.841 at the GKMC bounds), against the robust profile statistic m(0) = 7.300. The robust statistic at zero is not smaller than the homoskedastic one, so the gap between the robust and homoskedastic decisions comes from the critical value (chi-square(3) vs chi-square(1) or GKM19), not from heteroskedasticity. Remedy: a report-only claim on the existing metric, labelled descriptive and post hoc. It must not change the H3(b) decision rule or its primary set.

findings.text: The title promises more than the text delivers in two ways. (a) 'Card's (1995)': the 1995 chapter was never read, and every target is a WP 4483 (1993) number (Limitations, Sources). (b) 'Does growing up near a college raise schooling and earnings?' is the first-stage and reduced-form question, which needs only proximity independence, not exclusion. The paper never answers it in those terms: it reports the reduced forms only as restatements of the AR and CHR results for the return. Remedy: name the working paper in the title (e.g. 'Card's (1993, 1995)'), and either answer the title question explicitly from the first-stage and reduced-form claims with their Panel A or B labels, or retitle.
